newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo tea auction prices up on CIS, Gulf demand.
newsitem.headline: Colombo tea auction prices up on CIS, Gulf demand.

text.p: Tea prices rose at Wednesday's Colombo auction on strong demand from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and the Middle East, brokers said.
"The market was good. Most teas were dearer barring seasonal Uvas which fell on quality," said Yshan Fernando of Eastern Brokers.
"The CIS was fairly active and there was demand for leafy teas from the Middle East despite tension in the Gulf."
Brokers Forbes and Walker said the anticipated gross auction average price for the 4.3 million kg on offer should rise to 117 rupees per kg ($2.08) from 116.87 rupees per kg last week.
The next auction is on September 24-25 when 4.7 million kg will be on offer.
At last week's auction, prices of Sri Lanka's distinct low-grown teas fell after U.S. missile attacks on Iraq unnerved buyers, brokers said.
Earlier this month the U.S. earlier this month launched missile strikes on air defence targets in southern Iraq in retaliation for Baghdad's military advance into Kurdish areas.
